text: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models Predict outcomes. Learn from interaction. Improve the next decision. Framework · Domains · Results · Quick Start · Citation · 简体中文 RSI-Anything is a domain-general framework that turns world-model predictions and interaction feedback into recursive self-improvement. Built on JEPA-Anything , it connects candidate generation, prediction-guided selection, external evaluation and learning in a shared process. The paper applies this process to code repair, GUI interaction, laboratory planning, reaction optimization and immune science . Each domain supplies its own state, actions, prediction targets and feedback, while using the same cycle of proposing candidates, anticipating consequences, evaluating selected actions and retaining improvements for subsequent rounds. From the predictive foundation of JEPA-Anything to recursive self-improvement across domains. Propose → Predict → Select → Evaluate → Learn → Retain. A policy or workflow proposes actions; the world model predicts their consequences; selected actions receive external feedback. The resulting experience supports learning and evaluation, and the retained system guides the next round. The framework connects prediction-guided interaction with persistent improvements in policies and scientific workflows. View the framework PDF . Domain adapters connect the shared workflow to each task's states, action space and external feedback. Results across domains. See benchmark settings for task definitions, comparison protocols and metric interpretation: Figure 2. Prediction-guided code repair and benchmark comparisons. The figure connects the repair workflow ( a ) with CodeContests success, prediction quality and feedback use ( b–d ), and results on APPS Introductory and LiveCodeBench ( e–f ). The policy proposes four revisions per round, with up to three feedback rounds. Online tests provide repair feedback; final success is measured on the benchmark's evaluation tests. Results are averaged over three seeds. APPS Introductory and LiveCodeBench v6 extend the repair evaluation to 1,000 and 1,055 problems. Methods share the initial program and ReasonFlux-Coder-7B policy for each problem and seed; public tests guide repair and the complete official suite determines final success. Mean full-test success across three seeds reaches 46.37% and 33.05% , respectively. Mean actions decrease from 5.30 to 3.21 , and repeated clicks fall from 237 to 0 . Success requires all checkbox states to match the instruction and the form to be submitted, within 120 seconds and eight actions. OSWorld extends the GUI evaluation to desktop tasks. RSI-Anything improves task success by 18.4% relative to the initial agent and 5.5% relative to RLAnything ; RLAnything improves by 12.3% relative to the initial agent. See GUI results for controller definitions, evaluation cohorts and complete tables, and OSWorld settings for the desktop comparison. On Linux, follow the task guide to prepare .venv-code-repair or .venv-gui , and set runtime paths and GPU assignments in the recipe. Then launch the corresponding workflow: # Code repair rsi assets code_repair --profile full --output assets rsi plan --config configs/code_repair/default.json rsi run --config configs/code_repair/default.json # GUI interaction rsi plan --config configs/gui/default.json rsi run --config configs/gui/default.json See assets for downloads and offline preparation, and workflow design for stage interfaces.
